question: Is a 501(c)(3) DAF sponsoring organization a GLBA 'financial institution' (15 U.S.C. 6809(3); 16 CFR 314.2(h)), and is a donor who contributes to a DAF a 'consumer' obtaining a 'financial product or service ... primarily for personal, family, or household purposes'? In particular: does holding, investing and granting irrevocably contributed assets on a donor's advice constitute an activity 'financial in nature' under 12 U.S.C. 1843(k)?
why_unresolvable_internally: Turns on statutory interpretation with no located FTC/CFPB guidance, enforcement action or case addressing DAF sponsors; the charitable gift is irrevocable (sponsor owns assets per 26 U.S.C. 4966(d)(2)) which cuts against a consumer financial relationship, while investment/advisory and custody-like features cut in favour. Agents cannot give legal opinions.
lowest_cost_resolution: One scoped memo from a privacy/financial-services attorney (1-3 hours) answering this plus OQ-201..OQ-203 together; alternatively ask two prospective sponsors what position their counsel has taken.
blocks: GLBA applicability classification; REQ-GLBA-001..REQ-GLBA-016; privacy-notice design

question: If a nonprofit DAF sponsor is a GLBA financial institution, does the FTC have Safeguards Rule (16 CFR 314) enforcement jurisdiction over it, given 15 U.S.C. 6805(a)(7) assigns FTC enforcement 'under the Federal Trade Commission Act' and 15 U.S.C. 44 limits 'corporation' to for-profit entities (applied at the pleading stage in FTC v. Grand Canyon Education, D. Ariz. Aug 2024 and Mar 2025; case later voluntarily dismissed by the FTC, no appellate ruling)? Is there any other agency with GLBA safeguards authority over such a sponsor?
why_unresolvable_internally: Contested legal point: one reading is that GLBA's own grant gives FTC reach over any non-agency-supervised financial institution; the other is that FTC Act jurisdictional limits are incorporated. Only one secondary report of a district-court decision was located and it concerned FTC Act Section 5, not GLBA.
lowest_cost_resolution: Same counsel memo as OQ-200; counsel to check for FTC staff opinions or consent orders involving nonprofit financial institutions.
blocks: Whether Safeguards Rule is legal (sponsor) vs contractual/voluntary (Unbound)

question: Would the legal entity operating Unbound in production (currently Echelon Foundry, LLC, a for-profit) itself be a 'financial institution' under 16 CFR 314.2(h) - e.g., by providing data processing for financial data (12 CFR 225.28(b)(14)), acting as an account servicer, or as a donor-facing branded DAF platform - such that the Safeguards Rule applies to it directly and 314.1(b) brings in customer information received from sponsors?
why_unresolvable_internally: Requires a legal characterisation of a business model not yet fixed (white-label technology provider vs branded donor-facing platform vs administrator); FTC's 'significantly engaged' test is fact-specific and the FTC has not published guidance on DAF platforms.
lowest_cost_resolution: Counsel memo once the operating model and contracting entity are chosen; pending that, adopt the Safeguards Rule elements as a design baseline (no legal conclusion needed to do so).
blocks: Legal vs contractual classification of all REQ-GLBA Safeguards rows for Unbound

question: Does CFPB Regulation P (12 CFR 1016) reach nonprofit DAF sponsors (the Consumer Financial Protection Act's 'person' has no for-profit limitation) such that privacy notices and opt-out rules apply to donor information, and if so does the annual-notice exception apply?
why_unresolvable_internally: Depends on OQ-200 (whether a DAF is a consumer financial product) and on CFPB/FTC enforcement allocation for nonbank privacy; no guidance located.

question: Which bank partners (ODFI, disbursement, custody) will Unbound or its sponsors use, and what security/assurance terms will they require from Unbound: SOC 1 vs SOC 2 (type, scope, period), right to audit, incident-notice windows, subcontractor notice, examination access, SIG/questionnaire format, insurance?
why_unresolvable_internally: Contract terms are bank-specific and not public; TPRM guidance tells banks what to consider, not what each bank will demand.
lowest_cost_resolution: Ask one target bank's vendor-management team for their standard third-party due-diligence request list and model security addendum (often shareable under NDA before contracting).
blocks: REQ-BANK-*; REQ-TPRM-*; SOC report scoping decisions

question: Will Unbound contract directly with any bank such that it is a 'bank service provider' (Bank Service Company Act, 12 U.S.C. 1867(c)) subject to 12 CFR 53.4 / FDIC / Fed incident-notification duties and potential examination, or will it only be a sponsor's Nacha TPSP with no direct bank contract?
why_unresolvable_internally: Depends on contracting structure not yet decided (UNB PAY-DEF-001 defers rail and bank selection).
lowest_cost_resolution: Owner decision on contracting structure, then a counsel confirmation of BSCA status (short).

question: For ACH, will Unbound act only as a Nacha Third-Party Service Provider (per CNV-PAY-001) or could any program make it a Third-Party Sender (with rules-compliance audit and risk-assessment duties)? What ACH volume (aggregated across all sponsor clients) is projected, and when would the 2M-entry Supplementing Data Security threshold and fraud-monitoring duties attach?
why_unresolvable_internally: Role determination depends on bank agreements and Nacha rule text (subscription), and volume is a business forecast.
lowest_cost_resolution: Ask the prospective ODFI's ACH operations/compliance team to confirm the role classification in writing; obtain the current Nacha Operating Rules (paid subscription or via ODFI).

question: If card contributions are enabled (deferred from R1 per XID-ADV-001), who is the merchant of record (sponsor), will Unbound use only processor-hosted payment pages/iframes so cardholder data never touches Unbound systems, does Unbound qualify for SAQ A-level scope for its sponsors, and must Unbound itself provide a PCI DSS service-provider AOC (e.g., because its pages can affect the security of the payment page)?
why_unresolvable_internally: PCI scoping is decided by acquirers/QSAs, the SAQ A eligibility criteria changed in Jan 2025 and the related FAQ was reportedly revised in 2026; integration design not chosen.
lowest_cost_resolution: 30-minute scoping call with a QSA once processor and integration pattern are chosen; meanwhile design for hosted-field/redirect only.

question: Will any sponsor or Unbound market to, accept donors resident in, or monitor behaviour of individuals in the EU/UK (GDPR Art. 3(2)), and if so who is controller vs processor and is an Art. 27 representative needed?
why_unresolvable_internally: Business-scope decision plus legal characterisation; not determinable from requirements, which do not define geographic donor scope (UNB-REM-014).
lowest_cost_resolution: Owner decides geographic scope; if EU/UK in scope, short counsel review.

question: Which comprehensive state privacy laws apply (a) to each sponsor (several - CO, DE, NJ, OR, MD, MN per law-firm commentary - do not exempt 501(c)(3)s; thresholds vary) and (b) to Unbound as processor; and does any GLBA entity- or data-level exemption apply given OQ-200?
why_unresolvable_internally: State laws change frequently (2025 amendments removed GLBA entity-level exemptions in CT and MT); thresholds depend on resident counts per sponsor; statutes not read.
lowest_cost_resolution: Counsel or a maintained state-privacy tracker subscription; build a per-state applicability table keyed by resident counts that counsel signs off annually.

question: What breach-notification duties does Unbound owe as an entity that 'maintains' personal information on behalf of sponsors (state laws generally require notice to the data owner/licensee), and what contractual notice window will sponsors and banks require (e.g., 24-72 hours)?
why_unresolvable_internally: 50+ state statutes differ; contract windows are commercial terms.
lowest_cost_resolution: Counsel-approved notification matrix; ask first sponsors and banks for their standard window.

question: Will any sponsor, partner or bank customer be a NYDFS Part 500 covered entity, making Unbound a third-party service provider subject to its 500.11 policies (MFA, encryption, notice of cybersecurity events)?
why_unresolvable_internally: Depends on customer identity; DAF sponsors are not typically DFS licensees but bank or trust-company partners may be.
lowest_cost_resolution: Add one question to customer onboarding: 'Are you a DFS-regulated covered entity?'

question: For IRS compliance, which artefacts must the platform generate on the sponsor's behalf and retain for how long: 170(f)(8) and 170(f)(18) contemporaneous written acknowledgments, Form 990 Schedule D Part I data (6033(k)), Form 8282 dispositions of donated property, any 1099 information returns; and what retention period does the sponsor's tax advisor require given Treas. Reg. 1.6001-1(e)?
why_unresolvable_internally: Sponsor-specific tax positions; retention 'so long as material' needs a concrete period chosen by a tax advisor; Form 8282 and 1099 applicability not researched here.
lowest_cost_resolution: Tax advisor review of the generated-document catalogue (one session).

question: Allocation of OFAC sanctions-screening responsibility between sponsor (grantor, a U.S. person) and Unbound (a U.S. person that may 'facilitate' transactions): is screening by Unbound on the sponsor's behalf sufficient, and does Unbound need its own sanctions compliance program per OFAC's 2019 Framework?
why_unresolvable_internally: Legal allocation and facilitation analysis requires counsel; OFAC liability is strict (general knowledge, enforcement guidelines not re-read).
lowest_cost_resolution: Counsel review of the screening design already specified in Unbound (SPD-GRT-003) plus contract allocation language.

question: May Echelon Foundry use CIS Controls (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, commercial use needs approval), SCF (CC BY-ND 4.0 vs CC BY 4.0 conflict), CSA CCM and AICPA mapping spreadsheets in an internal control catalog that may later be published (repository is currently public) or embedded in a commercial product?
why_unresolvable_internally: Licence terms conflict across pages and commercial-use thresholds are vendor determinations.
lowest_cost_resolution: Email CIS (controlsinfo) and SCF Council for written confirmation of the intended use; until then anchor on NIST public material and reference other frameworks by identifier only.
blocks: framework-crosswalk-method anchor choice; any published control catalogue

question: Which assurance artefacts do prospective sponsors and institutional partners actually request (SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 certificate, CAIQ/STAR, SIG, penetration-test letter), and with what scope?
why_unresolvable_internally: Customer expectations are not public and vary; no sponsor relationship exists yet.
lowest_cost_resolution: Interview 3-5 prospective sponsors/partners or collect their vendor questionnaires.
blocks: Framework selection (ISO27001, CCM, SOC) and roadmap

question: Does any planned funds-flow (e.g., Unbound or an affiliate receiving, holding or transmitting donor or grant funds rather than the sponsor's bank) trigger state money-transmission licensing (and thereby NYDFS Part 500 / state examination)?
why_unresolvable_internally: Funds-flow design deferred (PAY-DEF-001); money-transmitter analysis is state-specific legal work outside this batch.
lowest_cost_resolution: Counsel review at the PAY-DEF-001 decision gate; keep the design principle that sponsor-owned bank accounts hold funds.
related: SRC-REG-052; SRC-REG-045; internal design answered (DF-ASR-2026-0D11; registers/question-dispositions.csv); legal applicability not assumed and external confirmation still required

question: Will bank partners, post-FFIEC CAT sunset, ask third parties for self-assessment evidence against a particular framework (NIST CSF 2.0 profile, CRI Profile, CISA CPGs) in addition to SOC reports?
why_unresolvable_internally: Bank-specific practice; agencies endorse no tool.
lowest_cost_resolution: Ask the target bank's TPRM team (same contact as OQ-204).
